title: Helloworld-to-Production SDK: retreat notes and quickstart blueprint
body:
Context and intent:
This doc captures outputs from a two-day internal retreat focused on compressing the typical SDK onboarding loop (first request -> production rollout) into a repeatable quickstart and a compact workshop. Goal: give new teams a 60–90 minute experiential path that results in a deployed sample app calling Redwood (hosted) with sensible telemetry, CI, and a fallback local mode.

What makes this different from other quickstarts:
- Emphasis on experiential learning (paired labs, failure injection stations) rather than step-by-step reading.
- Lightweight production checklist included (not just hello world).
- Telemetry contract baked into the quickstart so teams ship observable-by-default code.
- Local-first fallback harness so devs can iterate without cloud creds.

High-level agenda (2-day retreat condensed into an async quickstart):
- Phase 0: preflight (10–20 min)
  - Install CLI, get API key placeholder, clone repo.
  - Quick checklist script (scripts/check-preflight.sh) that verifies node/python/ruby runtime and Docker presence.
- Phase 1: hello flow (20–30 min)
  - Minimal sample app: weatherbot (frontend + serverless function) that calls Redwood chat/generation.
  - CLI command to run sample locally in dev mode (no real key): "redwood local-run --sample weatherbot".
- Phase 2: instrument (15–25 min)
  - Add telemetry events: request.sent, response.received, model.fallback, latency.ms.
  - Telemetry schema v0.3 (simple JSON lines): event, ts, request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms, success
- Phase 3: smoke & CI (15–30 min)
  - Add a lightweight smoke test that hits the stubbed endpoint and verifies shape of response.
  - GitHub Actions workflow: run tests on PR, run local smoke, and conditionally deploy to staging.
- Phase 4: rollout & rollback (20 min)
  - Show how to pin model versions in config and how to roll back to earlier pinned version when error rate > threshold.
- Phase 5: cost & SLO checkpoint (10 min)
  - Quick calculator to estimate per-1k-requests cost given tokens and batching settings.

Hands-on labs and stations (retreat-style metaphors preserved):
- Failure-injection station: simulate 5xxs and KV-cache misses, observe fallback routing to cheaper model.
- Secrets & identity station: demo ephemeral API keys via CLI and KMS-local-mock for on-prem parity.
- Latency tuning station: change batching window and measure p50/p95 on a replay harness.
- Mini-eval station: add a prompt-suite of 6 cases and run a simple regression check comparing two model variants.

Sample flows (concise):
- Flow A: Local dev -> Redwood stub -> local fallback -> success (fast path).
- Flow B: Local dev -> hosted model -> high latency -> automatic route to warmed ded<->fallback variant.
- Flow C: CI -> staging -> canary (5%) -> rollout (gradual) -> monitoring trigger -> automatic rollback.

Telemetry contract (v0.3) quick reference (intended to be copy-paste friendly):
- Fields (all snake_case): event, ts_iso, request_id, user_id?, model, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms, success_bool, error_code?, route, sample_app
- Recommended volumes: keep event sample rate 1.0 for request.sent and response.received, 0.2 for debug.trace events.
- Retention and privacy note: PII should never be included; redact prompt contents in telemetry by default (configurable sample/allowlist).

Quickstart file layout (repo skeleton):
- /samples/weatherbot/README.md (single page with run commands)
- /samples/weatherbot/src/server.js (or server.py)
- /samples/weatherbot/.redwoodrc (pin model, telemetry enabled)
- /scripts/check-preflight.sh
- /.github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml
- /tests/smoke/weatherbot_smoke.test.js

Developer experience bits:
- CLI helpers: redwood sdk init -> scaffolds sample, telem config, and CI workflow.
- Templates: minimal serverless handlers for Node/Python and a tiny React UI with example prompt flow.
- Error copy: include clear inline guidance for 401 (missing key), 429 (quota), 5xx (server).
- Offline mode: a tiny stub runner that returns canned responses with a note explaining divergence from hosted behavior.

Production checklist (short, for inclusion in quickstart as a "ship when" page):
- Telemetry events present and nav dashboard wired.
- CI smoke tests pass on main and PRs.
- Model pinned for initial rollout with clear variant mapping.
- Rate limiting and retry policy configured in SDK config.
- Secret rotation documented and verified via staging.
- Cost estimate reviewed and approved for expected QPS.
- Monitoring alerts: error rate > 2% (5m window), latency p95 > 2x baseline.

Open questions and tradeoffs surfaced at retreat:
- How opinionated should the SDK be about telemetry schema vs letting customers choose? Proposal: default schema + opt-out.
- Should quickstart include an A/B experiment harness or keep experiments in a separate advanced lab? Retreat leaned toward separate advanced lab.
- Level of default model pinning: pin major versions (e.g., "mistral-1.x") rather than exact commits to avoid frequent churn for new users.
- How to balance local-first fidelity vs not misleading users about hosted differences (include clear "differences" page).

Next steps (action items and owners):
- Priya: write the short README and preflight script (due 2024-10-08). (JIRA RDW-3201)
- Liam: scaffold GH Actions workflow and smoke tests (due 2024-10-15). (PR skeleton: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/457)
- Sofia: draft telemetry contract doc and example dashboard queries (due 2024-10-10).
- Ethan: implement local stub runner and offline mode docs (due 2024-10-12).
- Team: small playtest with 3 internal squads scheduled for 2024-10-21; gather feedback in retro doc.

Notes to self (informal brain-dump):
- Keep sample apps intentionally tiny; two patterns only (sync request-response and streaming/chat).
- Prefer copy-first examples (explicit strings) rather than heavy SDK abstractions in the quick path.
- Consider a 30-minute "mini-retreat" kit for remote teams: 5 prompts, 3 labs, 1 failure injection.
- Add a lightweight cost estimator UI snippet to the sample app so teams can see token burn in dev.

Appendix: links and references used during retreat:

End of document.

(If you want, I can convert this into a one-page printable workshop sheet or split into a README + lab scripts set.)
